item.title: Predicting next-week VIIRS fire detections in Bolivia: a reproducible benchmark with temporal and geographic evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weekly detection forecasts could help prioritize fire monitoring across Bolivia. We estimate the probability of at least one fire detection by the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) on the Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership satellite in each 0.05-degree cell during the following 7 days. Primary models were fixed before test scoring. Calibrated LightGBM, a gradient-boosted decision-tree model, reaches 2023-2025 temporal-test average precision (AP) of 0.323 (95% block-bootstrap interval 0.222-0.383), compared with 0.167 for climatology and 0.143 for persistence. Its paired AP gain over climatology is 0.1567 (0.0998-0.2179). A separately selected geographic model reaches AP 0.384 versus 0.181 for persistence in regions excluded from fitting. In the temporal-test population, reviewing the highest-ranked 5% and 10% of eligible area would have covered 38.4% and 55.8% of cell-weeks with detections. Probabilities still overestimate detection frequency in the highest-probability group. Retrospective rainfall provides no clear AP improvement; the primary validation comparisons for vegetation, land cover and their combination are inconclusive. Positive secondary or exploratory intervals do not change those decisions. Evaluation requires complete target and recent-history observations and measures satellite detections, not individual fires, causes or burned area. Prospective evaluation should archive inputs at each weekly issue and measure ranking, calibration and the usefulness of selected cells for monitoring decisions.
item.dc:creator: Victor Hugo Cuellar Flores

item.title: A Jump-Diffusion Model of Home Price Dynamics and Neighborhood Change
item.description: arXiv:2611.08956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a dynamical model that links the fluctuations of individual home prices to changes in the full distribution of home prices in an urban area. We model the price of an individual home as a jump-diffusion stochastic differential equation. To capture the dynamic and hyper-local economic conditions that drive the residential real estate market, we allow all parameters to depend on both time and neighborhood. In the mean-field limit, we derive the associated Fokker-Planck partial integro-differential equation (PIDE) governing the evolution of the home price distribution in a neighborhood. We quantify spatial heterogeneity within a city by using the Wasserstein-2 distance to compare home price distributions across the city's neighborhoods. We validate our model using data from Boston, Massachusetts as a case study.
item.dc:creator: Ashley Peake, Adam Gilbert-Diamond, Anette E. Hosoi

item.title: Slow structures, fast degrees of freedom, and the morphology of chess openings
item.description: arXiv:2611.09710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chess openings naturally separate into slow and fast degrees of freedom: pawns evolve through irreversible moves, whereas pieces can be rapidly reorganized within the resulting structure. We exploit this separation to construct a quantitative morphology of opening space. From a catalogue of 3810 named variations, 1749 reach a common depth of $N=10$ plies, corresponding to 619 distinct positions and only 435 joint pawn structures. We characterize these positions through observables measuring pawn commitment and spatial organization, blockade and tension, and piece activity and centralization. Their partial independence reveals a multidimensional opening space and in order to explore its structural organization, we construct a network whose nodes are distinct White pawn structures, connected when a single pawn move or capture transforms one into another. Remarkably, 139 of the 149 observed structures belong to a single connected component containing $98\%$ of all positions. This network exhibits a statistically significant modular organization, with eight communities whose representative structures correspond to familiar pawn formations. Rather than forming isolated categories, these formations emerge as distinct regions of a connected structural landscape. Our approach thus complements the traditional opening taxonomy by revealing similarities between differently named openings and providing a quantitative basis for comparing the positions they produce.
item.dc:creator: Marc Barthelemy, Manlio De Domenico

item.title: Scarce or Missed Opportunities? Structural Peers and Latin America's Diversification Frontier
item.description: arXiv:2611.09727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Latin America's limited export upgrading is often attributed to failures to seize available diversification opportunities. We distinguish two possibilities: countries failed to realize opportunities demonstrated by structurally similar economies, or upgrading-oriented options were scarce within this peer-revealed set. Using export data for 105 countries from 1962 to 2024, we construct country-specific opportunity sets with an imitation-density measure associated with subsequent product entry. Latin America's deficit arose mainly from scarce upgrading-oriented candidates rather than weak aggregate conversion. Conversion rates matched the global benchmark, but regional frontiers contained few manufacturing products and almost no higher-complexity manufacturing candidates and, unlike East and Southeast Asia, did not shift toward them over time. An illustrative decomposition associates most of the regional upgrading-entry gap with candidate availability. The findings imply that industrial policy should expand feasible upgrading pathways rather than focus only on converting existing opportunities.
item.dc:creator: Saangkeub Lee, Dawoon Jeong, Wonsub Eum, Jeong-Dong Lee

item.title: Regime change in a model for political opinion dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.09742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Political crises involving a series of violent events are the rule rather than the exception in history. Here, we use a minimal opinion dynamics model to describe regime change as a contested transition between dominant shared ideas in a society. New opinions spread with a cumulative advantage, and agents do not return to opinions they held before, resulting in recurrent boom-and-bust dynamics without tuned parameters. During a transition, opinion changes grow approximately exponentially and then saturate in the finite system, declining approximately linearly as spreading is limited by the shrinking interfaces between opinion groups. We compare qualitative features of these transitions with historical data of political violence, used as an empirical proxy for contested transitions. A permutation test shows that violent events cluster in time in the dense Chinese and US records. Around their peaks, violent events rise in an accelerating way and then decline; in the Chinese data, the decline is consistent with the approximately linear decline in the model. We also use a fragmentation measure that serves as an early warning signal for transitions in the model. Overall, the patterns in the empirical data and the dynamical behavior of the model could contribute to a better understanding of long-term historical processes.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Jochim, Stefan Bornholdt

item.title: Effects of a Nuclear Detonation in Low Earth Orbit
item.description: arXiv:2611.09827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: More than 13,000 satellites operate in low Earth orbit (LEO), and concern has grown that nuclear weapons could be used in space to target them. Beyond the initial X-ray burst, electrons released by radioactive fission products can become trapped in Earth's magnetic field, repeatedly exposing satellites as an artificial radiation belt. Here we couple prompt radiation, electron trapping and belt evolution to satellite failures, collisions and atmospheric drag. For a 1-Mt detonation at 500km over the South Atlantic, repeated belt exposure disables approximately 98% of modeled satellites within one week in our central case. Tripling the assumed radiation tolerance delays widespread failure by only days: approximately 97% are still disabled within two weeks. The loss of maneuverability sharply increases collision risk, with approximately 20 collisions expected within two years. Drag removes many disabled spacecraft from lower altitudes, but replacement satellites could remain exposed to radiation and debris for years. These findings show how a single detonation could devastate orbital infrastructure and support efforts to prevent the deployment and use of nuclear weapons in space.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Petersen, Hong Qin, Sarah Thiele, S\'{e}bastien Philippe

item.title: Online and Survey Representations of Well-Being: Coherence and Cross-Source Correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2611.08510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Digital traces may complement population surveys in the measurement of well-being, but the two sources do not necessarily capture identical constructs. We compare the Human Flourishing Geographic Index (HFGI) with World Values Survey and European Social Survey measures across three domains using structural equation models. The results show strong within-source coherence and construct-specific cross-source correspondence. Cross-source convergence varies across domains; the observed pattern is consistent with stronger correspondence where the underlying indicators are more closely aligned conceptually. Near-perfect agreement would be unexpected, since surveys elicit standardized self-reports, whereas HFGI captures naturally occurring public expressions. HFGI should therefore be viewed as a distinct but empirically connected measurement system that complements survey-based evidence on well-being.
item.dc:creator: Stefano M. Iacus, Giuseppe Porro, Haodong Qi

item.title: Dynamic signatures of collective knowledge through navigation in a network with semantic structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.08812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: What distinguishes how humans navigate an information network like Wikipedia from what the underlying graph structure and language statistics alone predict? To study human collective navigation, we analyze 70,770 human trajectories through Wikispeedia, an online game where players navigate between articles to reach a target. To compare groups of trajectories rather than individual ones, we merge all trajectories leaving or entering a given article into a Flow Tree. Flow Trees compress collections of trajectories into hierarchies of group splits. We build forward and reverse Flow Trees for 815 of the most commonly traversed articles, representing divergence and convergence, respectively. We compare humans against four random-walker null models, either unweighted or weighted by graph structure, word frequency, or semantic similarity to target. Human Flow Trees are deeper with longer trunks and later splits, indicating players stay together longer than random walkers, whose Flow Trees tend to fan out immediately. An article's degree predicts 51.3-70.9% of the variation in Flow Tree branching factor for random walkers, but only 24.1-36.2% for humans. Taking what graph structure fails to predict as a two-dimensional coordinate system, we define four article types (beacons, funnels, forks, and corridors), distinguished by how humans enter and exit them. These human-defined types are not explained by out-degree or title-word frequency are, and are not recovered by any random walker. A fifth null model, built from first-order human click preferences, partially reproduces human Flow Tree shape but differs significantly in how much of that shape degree explains. We consider collective knowledge to be the structure shared by players who never communicate, beyond what graph structure imposes. It comprises first-order click preferences and a significant component that extends across clicks.
item.dc:creator: Abby Bertics, Elizabeth R. Chrastil, Jean M. Carlson

item.title: Incentive Pathologies in a Live LLM Agent Arena: An Empirical Study of Concentration, Reward-Rule Implementation Discrepancy, and Network Dilution
item.description: arXiv:2611.09445v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We audit one live LLM agent arena (AITRAP; 22 autonomous agent seats, ~96,000 reasoning nodes) over nine days (Oct 16-25, 2026), during which the platform deployed two bundled incentive changes: a progressive tax reform (V2.9.3, Oct 19) and a seed-inversion with explorer-side action update (V3.0, Oct 21). These serve as before-and-after markers, not cleanly isolated interventions. Four exploratory predictions are tested against ten data frames (F1-F10) using the Gini coefficient, Top-K concentration share, code-level reconstruction of the continuation-bonus mechanism, and the Mann-Kendall trend test. The Gini analysis is inconclusive at 95% confidence (bootstrap intervals straddle 0.7). The Top-4 node-activity-score share falls from 97.2% (Oct 19, pre-V2.9.3) to 49.4% (Oct 25, post-V3.0; 56.7% under a merge-seat assumption). The continuation bonus, announced as depth-based x10, resolves at code level to a four-condition anti-abuse gate paying x2.85 in the typical case and permanently blocking the self-continuation it superficially rewards; the gate was active ~40 hours before the V3.0 announcement. The events-per-node ratio declines significantly (Mann-Kendall S=-45, z=-3.94, p=8.3e-5) from 7.36 to 7.069. We discuss implications for incentive designers, the announcement-implementation gap, and public peer review as an event record.
item.dc:creator: Lei Zhenbing, Lei Chang

item.title: Resolving non-neutrality across scales in a hyperdiverse tropical forest
item.description: arXiv:2611.09479v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Different ecological processes operate at different spatial and temporal scales. Macroscopic regularities can therefore be captured by descriptions that ignore microscopic details, even when those details are mechanistically relevant to ecological processes. Here, we develop a framework inspired by statistical mechanics to track interspecific spatial correlations under spatial coarse-graining. To do so we combine random-matrix filtering with a spatially explicit neutral model. Applying this approach to eight censuses of the Barro Colorado Island tropical forest, we observe a continuous crossover from an interacting to an effectively neutral organization. Below a few tens of metres (20--35~m), the empirical correlation spectrum differs from neutral expectations, revealing scale-dependent species-specific structure. Part of this structure can be attributed to environmental heterogeneity. However, residual spatial associations provide candidate signatures of biotic interactions or other unmeasured ecological, non-neutral processes. With increasing spatial coarse-graining, empirical and neutral correlation spectra progressively converge, and above the crossover scale the neutral model provides an accurate description of the measured collective organization. Neutrality thus emerges as an effective description of the collective organization of the forest above a characteristic scale, without implying that species are equivalent at the individual level. Our framework provides an operational way to locate that scale.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Zgaga, Pablo Villegas, Tancredi Caruso, Tommaso Gili

item.title: Asynchronous Barter, Periodic Reconciliation: Evidence for a Scale-Free Commercial Network in the Indus Valley Civilization
item.description: arXiv:2604.23582v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Harappan Civilization (c.\ 2600--1900 BCE) achieved extraordinary standardization across a vast region without clear evidence of centralized rule. We propose that it was a merchant commonwealth organized as a scale-free commercial network, with AP2PBS (Asynchronous Peer-to-Peer Barter Settlement) and the Unicorn Logistics Cartel (ULC) serving as inferential model labels for its coordinating institutions. Four lines of evidence support this interpretation. (1) \textbf{Statistical}: Unicorn $\alpha \approx 1.8$, offering stand with a power-law distribution with $\alpha \approx 2.3$--$2.6$, while seal counts at sites follow $\alpha \approx 1.55$; all fit heavy-tailed power-law better than exponential alternatives. (2) \textbf{Attribute correlations}: non-random associations between offering stands and anatomical attributes, including Cram\'er's V patterns across market tiers, are consistent with deliberate institutional design of visual confirmation bundles. (3) \textbf{Archaeological}: seal evolution, contextual distributions, and warehouse logistics support the operational requirements of long-distance asynchronous exchange. (4) \textbf{Architectural}: Mohenjo-daro's halls, bath, warehouses, and cart-compatible gridiron are consistent with infrastructure for commerce and coordination. Taken together, these findings are consistent with AP2PBS and ULC as models of how independent participants could standardize authentication, exchange value asynchronously, and coordinate across distance without a hierarchical state. Scale-free topology also offers a testable explanation for both Harappan longevity and its vulnerability to hub failure and cascading decline. The argument is inferential: the archaeological record does not directly identify AP2PBS or ULC by name, but its statistical, material, and architectural patterns are compatible with this decentralized commercial model.
item.dc:creator: Mahesh T C

item.title: Giant strongly biconnected components of directed networks: a generating function approach
item.description: arXiv:2608.25562v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Strongly connected components (SCCs) characterize modular structure in directed networks but are fragile to single node failures. We study strongly biconnected components (SBCs), which are the set of nodes in which every node pair remains mutually reachable after the removal of any single node, as a more robust notion of connectivity. Using a generating function formalism, we derive the size of the giant SBC and analyze its percolation behavior under random node and link removal. We show that the giant SBC emerges at the same threshold as the giant SCC but grows more slowly, consistent with previous findings for undirected networks. We also applied our theoretical framework to real-world biological networks including gene regulatory networks and neural connectome. Our framework provides insight into the interplay between connectivity, redundancy, and robustness in complex directed systems.
item.dc:creator: Minsoo Yang, Reinhard Laubenbacher, Byungjoon Min

item.title: Two preregistered datasets on production-type labelling in the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform: multi-fuel reporting, register vintages, persistent misclassification, and cross-product consistency
item.description: arXiv:2609.16152v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The ENTSO-E Transparency Platform is the single mandated publication point for European electricity market data, and three of its data items carry a production-type label. Commission Regulation (EU) No 543/2013 Article 16(1)(a) requires actual generation output per generation unit but does not mention production type; the label on that item is ENTSO-E's own addition through the schema, and Article 5(d) delegates the classification of production types to a Manual of Procedures. This data descriptor documents two preregistered datasets that measure what that classification does in practice, along four axes: simultaneous multi-fuel reporting, type change between capacity-register vintages, persistent misclassification without type change, and cross-product consistency between the per-unit and the aggregated series. Criteria were locked and checksummed before measurement, thresholds are derived from measured noise rather than chosen, and what did not survive is recorded: six claims are withdrawn, three of them from published versions of the datasets themselves. Across 2191 documents covering 199 generation units in three bidding zones where biomass co-firing is documented in a dated primary source, no unit carries two production types in the same document. One practical warning applies to every user of the hourly series: all of it carries curveType A03, a step curve in which a missing position means the previous value holds rather than that data are absent. A parser that sums only the points listed under-reports energy unevenly, by 22.6 percent for one Finnish unit in 2021.
item.dc:creator: Eirik Botten Nicolaysen (EcoDeco AS)

item.title: Hurricane recovery gaps lie in reconnection, not local restart
item.description: arXiv:2610.17550v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Climate-intensified hurricanes disrupt urban mobility, yet whether recovery is equitable across the rural-urban gradient is unclear. Analyzing device-based mobility for Hurricanes Helene and Milton, we find local activity restarted within approximately 4.5 days in both storms, whereas reconnection to the outside world took 5 days in coastal-urban Florida but 11 in inland-rural Appalachia. The gap lies in external reconnection, not local restart, implying planners should target rural isolation.
item.dc:creator: Angelina Liu, Mengqiu Cao, Sen Pei, Qing Yao

item.title: Feedback percolation on complex networks
item.description: arXiv:2603.22089v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Traditional percolation theory assumes static microscopic rules, limiting its ability to describe real-world complex systems where macroscopic order actively regulates local interactions. Here, we introduce feedback percolation, an unified framework that dynamically couples the microscopic activation probability to the macroscopic size of the giant component. We show that this simple feedback mechanism produces a rich variety of behaviors both analytically and numerically. Depending on the feedback functions, the system exhibits explosive discontinuous jumps, hybrid transitions, limit-cycle oscillations, and routes to chaos, absent in classical percolation. Our findings establish that macroscopic feedback provides a unifying physical mechanism for phenomena ranging from self-regulating oscillations to systemic infrastructure collapse.
item.dc:creator: Hoseung Jang, Ginestra Bianconi, Byungjoon Min
